name: Banana cake
origin: Rose to popularity in the United States after baking soda and baking powder became household staples in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, as a way to use very ripe bananas rather than discard them.

ingredients.note: water fraction of mashed ripe banana at 120% of flour mass, split by USDA raw-banana composition (~75% water)
non-water fraction (starch, sugars) of the same mashed banana
ripe banana's own mild acidity is enough for a bicarbonate-only leavening, without a separate acid ingredient

process.name: cream butter and sugar
process.description: beat butter and sugar until light

process.name: add eggs and banana
process.description: beat in eggs, then the mashed banana

process.name: fold in flour
process.description: fold in flour, leavening and salt

notes: Mashed banana's real water content (USDA FoodData Central, raw banana: ~74.9 g water per 100 g) is split into its own liquid-role line, the same technique used for carrot cake above. 120% banana relative to flour is a representative, banana-forward ratio; real recipes vary with how ripe (and therefore how concentrated) the fruit is.
